title: Basil Oil
description: Her signature — jewel-green finishing oil for tomato soup, eggs, burrata, anything.

steps.text: Blanch the basil in boiling water for 10 seconds, shock in ice water, then squeeze bone dry.
steps.why: Ten seconds of heat kills the enzymes that would turn the oil muddy brown, and the ice shock locks the chlorophyll bright green.

steps.text: Blend the basil with the oil and a pinch of salt until vivid green, about 45 seconds.
Strain through a fine sieve without pressing the solids.
steps.why: Pressing forces fine particles through and clouds the oil. Let gravity work and you get a jewel-clear green.

notes.title: Storage
notes.body: Stays vividly green about 2 days in the fridge. Bring to room temperature before drizzling — cold oil sits in blobs.

plating: Always last, always off the heat — drizzle in a spiral so it pools in emerald islands instead of blending in.
elevations: Swap a third of the basil for parsley — steadier green, softer flavor.
